findings.title: linear re-serialization in fitObjectionsByRound
findings.action: Replace the per-round scan with a binary search over the start index, which measures the same serialization in O(log N) steps.
findings.disposition_rationale: Real but out of this slice's licence. The spec closes the algorithm with a Chosen: decision and pseudocode (section 4, Phase 1) that mandates measuring the whole candidate suffix on each step, and names a divergent measurement as the failure mode the two-phase design exists to prevent. The common path costs exactly one serialization (the full array fits on the first iteration) and a realistic over-cap corpus costs tens; the mint is best-effort at run close and gates nothing. Recorded as discovered scope for its own ticket rather than diverging from a settled decision mid-build.

findings.title: unguarded regex match in the rounds reader-compatibility assertion
findings.action: Assert the match is non-null before reading .length so an Array.isArray regression fails with its own message.
findings.disposition_rationale: Valid and cheap. Fixed in 81114db3: the match is bound to roundLines, asserted non-null, and only then counted, so the guard fails with its own message instead of a TypeError on .length.

findings.finding_id: plugin/skills/faff/bin/lib/judge-trail.js::dropped rounds recorded as a count rather than by round number
findings.title: dropped rounds recorded as a count rather than by round number
findings.action: No action: the retained member's own first entry carries the first retained round number.
findings.disposition_rationale: The amputation is already reconstructible: judge-history --rounds returns the member, whose first entry's round is the first retained round, alongside the manifest's dropped_rounds count. The over-cap test asserts both (first retained round 5 > original 1, last retained 8, dropped_rounds 4). The non-contiguity the finding cites comes from FAFF-1131's corrupt-round skip, which this diff does not touch, and the spec closes the manifest surface at exactly two additive fields (section 3).

occurrences.title: dropped rounds recorded as a count rather than by round number

findings.finding_id: plugin/skills/faff/bin/lib/judge-trail.js::truncation marker readable as a size guarantee
findings.title: truncation marker readable as a size guarantee
findings.action: State at the manifest field that the marker reports dropped history, not boundedness.
findings.disposition_rationale: Valid reading of a real asymmetry the spec chose (section 4, single-residue-over-cap edge case: truncated:false with a blob over the cap). Fixed in 81114db3 with a comment at the field saying the marker is a history-completeness signal and never a size guarantee; no behaviour or field shape changed, so the spec's closed manifest surface holds.
